docs.title: Liminal Technical Writer Candidate Assignment
docs.text: Welcome to the Liminal Technical Writer Assignment & WebHelp Portal. This interactive documentation suite presents solutions for the Liminal Technical Writer Evaluation Assignment, hosted as a production-ready documentation site using MkDocs Material and deployed via GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
Liminal is a premier crypto wallet infrastructure provider enabling exchanges to manage hot wallets, automate fund transfers, and stake institutional digital assets securely. Technical documentation at Liminal bridges the gap between complex blockchain infrastructure, API schemas, security enforcement, and developer experience.

This documentation suite demonstrates a holistic approach to technical writing:

  1. Precision API Engineering Documentation (Q1): Formally specifying address risk screening integrations with security partner cube3.
  2. User-Centric Product Guide Redesign (Q2): Conducting an in-depth audit of the Solana Staking Guide and delivering a complete task-oriented rewrite.
  3. RESTful Architecture & API Standardization (Q3): Evaluating legacy non-REST endpoints and redesigning them according to modern REST standards, HTTP semantics, and RFC 7807 error specifications.
  4. Portfolio Showcase & Track Record (Q4): Highlighted technical documentation projects with clear scope breakdown and impact metrics.

docs.title: Assignment Navigation Hub
docs.text:
• Q1: Send Many Transaction API Documentation

    Documentation update for /sendmanytransaction incorporating cube3 threat screening, screeningFlag body parameters, 200 OK success schemas, and atomic 400 Bad Request rejection rules for high-risk addresses (> 80 risk score).

    View Q1 API Reference

  • Q2: Solana Staking Guide Audit & Rewrite

    8-point usability audit of Liminal's Solana Staking Guide, accompanied by a complete step-by-step rewritten developer and customer guide with state diagrams and troubleshooting tables.

    View Q2 Audit & Guide

  • Q3: RESTful API Redesign

    Architectural standardization of 3 non-REST legacy endpoints (/gettransfers, /sendmanytransaction, /getwalletbalance) into resource-oriented RESTful URIs with idempotency, status code matrix, and migration strategies.

    View Q3 REST Redesign

  • Q4: Work Samples & Portfolio

    Selected technical writing samples showcasing documentation for developer platforms, API references, architecture guides, and developer tooling.

    View Q4 Portfolio

docs.title: Technical Documentation Standards & Principles
docs.text:
All documentation produced in this submission adheres to the following core tenets:

  • Accuracy & Completeness: Every parameter, header, data type, and error response is explicitly defined without ambiguity.
  • Developer-First Ergonomics: Code examples are provided in cURL, Python, and Node.js with copy-paste readiness.
  • Visual Clarity: Complex control flows and state transitions are illustrated using Mermaid sequence & state diagrams.
  • Edge Case Governance: Clear guidance on failure modes, error handling, risk thresholds, and fallback behaviors.

docs.title: GitHub Pages Hosting & Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide provides step-by-step instructions for hosting and deploying this MkDocs WebHelp Portal on GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Deployment Architecture
docs.text:
The documentation site is built using MkDocs with the Material for MkDocs theme. Deployment can be executed in two ways:

  1. Automated Continuous Integration (CI/CD) via GitHub Actions (Recommended for production).
  2. Manual Command Line Deployment using mkdocs gh-deploy.

docs.title: Method 1: Automated GitHub Actions Workflow (Recommended)
docs.text: An automated GitHub Actions workflow file is included in .github/workflows/deploy.yml. Whenever changes are pushed to the main branch, GitHub Actions will build the static HTML site and publish it to the gh-pages branch automatically.

docs.title: Setup Instructions
docs.text:
1. Push Repository to GitHub: Ensure your local workspace is initialized as a git repository and pushed to your GitHub account: 

    git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit: Liminal Technical Writing Submission"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/Assignment_LM.git
git push -u origin main

  2. Configure GitHub Repository Settings:

    • Go to your repository on GitHub: https://github.com/Rajwar88/Assign.
    • Click Settings > Pages (under Code and automation).
    • Under Build and deployment:
      • Source: Select Deploy from a branch (or GitHub Actions).
      • Branch: Select gh-pages branch, / (root) folder.
    • Click Save.

  3. Verify Deployment: Once the GitHub Action completes, your site will be live at: https://rajwar88.github.io/Assign/

docs.title: Method 2: Manual CLI Deployment
docs.text: If you prefer to publish directly from your local terminal using Python and MkDocs:

docs.title: Step 1: Install Dependencies
docs.text:
Ensure Python 3 and MkDocs Material are installed: 

pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material

docs.title: Step 2: Test Local Preview
docs.text:
Run the local dev server to verify all pages render cleanly: 

mkdocs serve
Open your browser to http://127.0.0.1:8000 to preview the site.

docs.title: Step 3: Publish to GitHub Pages
docs.text:
Run the gh-deploy command: 

mkdocs gh-deploy --clean
This command automatically builds the static site into site/, commits it to the gh-pages branch, and pushes it to GitHub.

docs.title: Local Build Verification
docs.text:
To verify that the site builds with zero broken links or missing assets, execute: 

mkdocs build --strict
If the command finishes with exit code 0, your site is 100% compliant and ready for production hosting!

docs.title: Create transaction requests
docs.text:
POST https://api-sdk.lmnl.dev/api/wallet/send-many-transaction

API Reference Update — Security & Compliance Integration

Feature Update: Integrated cube3 Security Inspector API for real-time destination address screening. New Parameter: screeningFlag (boolean) added to Send-Many-Transaction-Object-Request. Behavior: Automatically screens destination addresses for cyber, fraud, and compliance threats. Blocks the transaction if any destination address has a combined Risk Score > 80 and returns HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity (RISK_SCREENING_FAILED).

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This API is a request to execute a single or multiple transactions from a v1 withdrawal wallet to the specified destination address(es). EVM chains support transfers to a single address, while UTXO chains support transfers to one or more addresses. You can transfer funds in either native coin or token in a single request.

For opt-in asset chains like XRP and Stellar (XLM), use wallet.transactionType = "enableToken" to establish a one-time trust line before sending or receiving token assets.

With the integration of Cube3 Security Inspector, destination addresses can be evaluated for security threats (such as sanctioned entities, drainer contracts, and malicious actors) prior to broadcasting transactions on-chain.

docs.title: Parameter Guidelines & Validation Rules
docs.text:
Accepted parameter values:

  1. The transactions.recipientsData.recipients[].address parameter must have a valid address length (> 0). It will not accept any null value or empty String value.
  2. The data type of transactions.recipientsData.recipients[].amount is updated to String and must be a positive decimal string. It will not accept empty string, null, or number value.
  3. The transactions.recipientsData.sequenceId parameter is a required unique tracking identifier (UUID format) generated by the client.
  4. [NEW] The screeningFlag parameter is a Boolean (true or false).
  5. When set to true, all destination addresses in transactions.recipientsData.recipients[] are evaluated via Cube3 Inspector API before broadcast.
  6. If any address has a combined Risk Score > 80, the transaction request is aborted and returns HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity with error code RISK_SCREENING_FAILED.
  7. When set to false or omitted, no screening takes place and standard payout rules apply.
  8. Asset Enablement (wallet.transactionType):
  9. Set to "enableToken" to create a trust line for non-native assets on XRP (RLUSD) or Stellar (USDC).
  10. When wallet.transactionType is "enableToken", transactions.recipientsData.recipients must be an empty array [].

docs.title: Optional Parameters
docs.text:
1. Address Screening (screeningFlag):
  2. screeningFlag: Set to true to activate automated pre-transaction destination address threat screening. Default is false.
  3. Using feeLevel and evmCustomfee:
  4. The feeLevel parameter is applicable for EVM chains (slow, market, aggressive, custom). Use only maxFeePerGas (Wei) if the coin value is BNB. Use both parameters for EIP-1559 chains.
  5. The maxPriorityFeePerGas (Wei) cannot be greater than maxFeePerGas (Wei).
  6. Use evmCustomfee object only when the feeLevel parameter is custom. Refer to the Retrieve estimated gas fees and rates API reference to get the required fee estimation rates.

docs.title: Parameter Reference Table
docs.text: Parameter Path Data Type Requirement Description wallet object Required Wallet details object (coin, walletId, allToken, tokenOptions). wallet.coin string Required Abbreviated cryptocurrency symbol (e.g., eth, btc, sol, bnb, xrp, xlm). wallet.walletId integer Required Unique identifier of the source withdrawal wallet. wallet.transactionType string Optional (Default: "transfer") Transaction operation type ("transfer" or "enableToken" for XRP/XLM trust lines). wallet.allToken boolean Optional Set to true when transferring non-native token assets. wallet.tokenOptions.tokenName string Optional Token symbol name (e.g., USDC, RLUSD). wallet.tokenOptions.tokenAddress string Optional Contract address (EVM) or <AssetCode>.<Issuer> (XRP) / <AssetCode>:<Issuer> (XLM). transactions.recipientsData.recipients array[object] Required Array of recipient objects (address, amount, data). Must be [] for enableToken. transactions.recipientsData.recipients[].address string Required Target destination wallet address. transactions.recipientsData.recipients[].amount string Required Positive decimal string representing transfer amount. transactions.recipientsData.sequenceId string Required Unique system sequence UUID generated by the client for tracking. screeningFlag boolean Optional (Default: false) [NEW] Controls pre-transaction Cube3 risk screening. feeLevel string Optional Gas fee tier (slow, market, aggressive, custom). evmCustomfee.maxPriorityFeePerGas string Optional Priority gas fee in Wei. evmCustomfee.maxFeePerGas string Optional Maximum gas fee in Wei.

docs.title: Q2: Solana Staking Guide — Comprehensive Audit & Rewritten Guide
docs.text:
This document provides a two-part technical evaluation of Liminal's Solana Staking Guide:

  1. Part A: In-Depth Audit & Points of Improvement — Structural, technical, and UX critique of the existing guide (/docs/stake-solana-assets-in-liminal-vaults).
  2. Part B: Rewritten Solana Staking Master Guide — A redesigned, step-by-step, task-oriented user guide for Liminal Dashboard users.

docs.title: Part A: In-Depth Audit & Points of Improvement
docs.text:
After reviewing Liminal’s existing Solana Staking Guide via live MCP documentation audit, 8 critical gaps were identified from the perspective of an institutional exchange operator using Liminal Vaults.

Below is the structured audit matrix detailing each gap, its operational impact, and recommended remedies:

docs.title: Audit Matrix
docs.text: # Improvement Area Identified Gap in Original Guide Recommended Technical & Documentation Remedy 1 Prerequisites & Rent-Exempt Reserve Does not specify that Solana requires a Rent-Exempt Minimum Reserve (~0.00228288 SOL) per stake account, plus transaction fee buffer (~0.005 SOL). Users attempting to stake 100% of their balance experience silent transaction failures. Add a prominent Prerequisites Checklist explicitly detailing mandatory minimum un-staked SOL reserves required for stake account creation and gas fees. 2 Solana Warm-Up & Cool-Down Epoch Lifecycle Omits explanation of Solana's Epoch Warm-Up (~2 days) and Unbonding Period (~2-day cool-down). Users expect immediate reward generation after clicking "Stake". Include a dedicated Staking State Machine Diagram explaining the Activating state, 2-day reward credit frequency, and epoch transition timing. 3 Multi-Sig & Cold Vault Quorum Workflow Cold storage and MPC vaults require multi-signature approval. The original guide treats staking as a single-click action, confusing institutional users whose vaults require threshold signoffs from secondary keyholders. Detail the Multi-Sig Quorum Approval Workflow, explaining how initiators and co-signers approve requests via the Vaults web platform and Mobile Co-Signer App. 4 Validator Partner & Commission Transparency Lacks clarity on the integrated validator partner (Figment), omitting details on validator commission rates, Figment Terms of Service acceptance, and reward yields (~6.42% APY). Provide explicit Figment Validator Integration guidance, including mandatory TOS signoff and yield expectations. 5 De-delegation & Unbonding Procedure Focuses solely on initiating a stake, omitting instructions for Unstaking (De-delegating), the 2-day cool-down epoch period, and withdrawing principal + rewards back to the main wallet. Add a complete Section for De-delegation & Withdrawals, detailing cool-down timing and rent-exempt SOL reclamation. 6 Visual Step-by-Step UI Guidance Uses placeholder images or lacks clear UI screenshots with callout indicators for Liminal Vaults navigation. Incorporate authentic Liminal UI Screenshots for wallet enablement, account creation, mobile co-signing, and delegation. 7 Rewards Calculator Tool Does not explain how exchange operations teams can estimate projected SOL yields prior to locking up capital. Add a Liminal Rewards Calculator guide detailing inputs (Amount, Duration, Asset Price, APR %) and projected yield outputs. 8 Troubleshooting & Error Recovery Contains no troubleshooting table for common UI errors (e.g. Single staking process limit, Insufficient SOL for Stake Account creation, Pending Co-Signer Timeout). Add a comprehensive Troubleshooting & FAQ reference table at the end of the guide.

docs.title: Part B: Rewritten Solana Staking Master Guide
docs.text:
DOCUMENT METADATA
Title: Staking Solana (SOL) Assets via Liminal Institutional Vaults
Audience: Exchange Operations, Custody Managers, Treasury Leads
Product: Liminal Dashboard / Vaults Staking Hub
Validator Partner: Figment
Last Updated: September 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Liminal’s Staking Hub allows institutional exchanges to stake SOL directly from warm MPC and cold vaults. Staking SOL enables you to earn network inflation rewards (~6.42% APY powered by Figment) while retaining full multi-signature custody of your underlying private keys.

Key staking parameters: - Reward Rate: ~6.42% APR (subject to network inflation dynamics). - Reward Credit Frequency: Every ~2 days (at epoch boundaries). - Unbonding Period: ~2 days (cool-down epoch before withdrawal). - Compounding: Rewards automatically compound within your dedicated Stake Account.

Custody Safety & Multi-Sig Rules

  • No Custody Loss: Liminal never acquires or retains custody of your staked assets at any time.
  • Single Process Rule: You can initiate only one staking process for a wallet at a time.
  • Immutable Stake Amount: Once staked, the delegation amount cannot be modified; additional stakes require a new staking account.

docs.title: Solana Rewards Calculator
docs.text:
Before delegating assets, you can calculate projected yields using the built-in Liminal Rewards Calculator:

  1. Log into Liminal Vaults.
  2. Navigate to Staking > Rewards Calculator.
  3. Fill in the parameters:
  4. Asset: Select SOL (Solana).
  5. Amount of Tokens: Enter your intended staking volume (e.g., 1,000 SOL).
  6. Staking Duration: Set target lockup period (e.g., 365 Days).
  7. Price of Asset: Enter current market price in USD.
  8. Rewards Rate (APR): Set network APR (~6.42%).
  9. The panel displays projected total rewards in both USD equivalent and native SOL.

docs.title: Solana Stake Account Lifecycle
docs.text:
Solana does not stake tokens directly from your primary vault address. Instead, Liminal creates a dedicated on-chain Stake Account funded by your wallet and delegates it to the Figment validator node.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Inactive: Fund & Create Stake Account
    Inactive --> Activating: Delegate to Figment (Submit Tx)
    note right of Activating
      Warm-Up Period: ~2 Days (1 Epoch)
      No yield earned during activation.
    end note
    Activating --> Active: Epoch Transition Complete
    note right of Active
      Active Staking State
      Rewards credited & auto-compounded every ~2 days.
    end note
    Active --> Deactivating: Initiate De-delegation (Unstake)
    note right of Deactivating
      Cool-Down Period: ~2 Days (1 Epoch)
      Tokens locked until epoch completes.
    end note
    Deactivating --> Inactive: Cool-Down Complete
    Inactive --> [*]: Withdraw Principal + Yield to Main Wallet

docs.title: Prerequisites Checklist
docs.text:
Before initiating a Solana staking transaction, verify your vault setup:

  • Staking Enabled for Org: Confirm your organisation has enabled Solana staking with Liminal (sales@lmnl.app).
  • Rent-Exempt Reserve: Maintain at least ~0.0023 SOL un-staked in the main wallet for on-chain stake account rent exemption.
  • Gas Fee Reserve: Preserve an additional ~0.005–0.01 SOL in liquid balance for future de-delegation and withdrawal gas fees.
  • Signing Quorum Ready: For MPC and multi-sig wallets, ensure required threshold initiators and signers are available to approve transaction requests via web or mobile app.

docs.title: Step 1: Enable Staking for your Solana Wallet
docs.text:
Once staking is activated for your organisation, enable the SOL asset chain in Liminal Vaults:

  1. Log into Liminal Vaults.
  2. Go to Staking.
  3. Locate SOL asset and select Start Staking.
  4. In the Wallet field, select your target Solana wallet.
  5. Check mark the Figment Terms of Service agreement.
  6. Select Enable Staking.
  7. Enter your Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) code and select Continue.
  8. Refresh the page to confirm the wallet is enabled for SOL staking.

docs.title: Step 2: Create an On-Chain Staking Account
docs.text:
A staking account is a dedicated sub-account created within your Solana wallet to manage staked funds, accumulate rewards, and process withdrawals.

  1. In the Staking dashboard, expand the SOL asset row.
  2. Select Create Account.
  3. Complete the form:
  4. Amount: Enter the SOL amount to transfer from your main wallet to the staking account.
  5. Note: Add a transaction description for auditing purposes.
  6. Select Next > Sign.

  1. Multi-Sig Quorum Signoff:
  2. Initiators: Log into Vaults web, find the pending transaction under Pending Actions, select Approve, and enter 2FA.
  3. Signers: Log into the Vaults Mobile App, locate the notification under Pending Approvals, and tap Approve.

Once quorum signoff is complete, the SOL amount is transferred to your newly created staking account.

docs.title: Step 3: Stake Solana Assets (Delegate to Figment)
docs.text:
Once the staking account is created and funded, delegate the assets to Figment:

  1. Go to Staking and expand the SOL asset.
  2. Locate your newly created staking account and select Stake.
  3. In the Note field, enter a description and click Next.
  4. Click Sign and enter your 2FA code.
  5. Complete the threshold multi-sig approval via Vaults Web / Mobile App as performed in Step 2.

  1. Upon successful broadcast, the staking balance displays as Activating.
  2. After ~2 days (epoch shift), the status updates to Active, and inflation rewards begin compounding automatically.

docs.title: Unstaking (De-delegating) & Principal Withdrawal
docs.text:
When you wish to return staked SOL back to your main liquid wallet balance:

  1. Navigate to Staking > expand SOL.
  2. Locate the target active staking account and click Unstake (De-delegate).
  3. Sign and complete multi-sig approval. Status shifts to Deactivating.
  4. Cool-Down Period: Wait approximately 2 days (until the current Solana epoch ends).
  5. Once the status updates to Inactive, select Withdraw to transfer the principal + accrued rewards back into your main wallet account.

docs.title: Troubleshooting & Common Support Inquiries
docs.text: Issue / Error Message Root Cause Resolution Step Insufficient SOL for Rent Exemption Attempted to stake entire wallet balance without leaving reserve for stake account creation (~0.0023 SOL). Reduce stake amount to leave at least 0.01 SOL liquid balance in the main wallet. Single Staking Process Limit Attempted to initiate a second staking request while a previous transaction is still pending approval. Complete or cancel the pending staking transaction before starting a new request. Staking status stuck in Activating Solana epoch boundary (~2 days) has not yet elapsed. Rewards and active delegation begin at epoch shift. Monitor epoch status under Staking dashboard. Pending Quorum Timeout Multi-sig initiators or mobile signers did not approve within the approval window. Re-initiate transaction and ensure co-signers approve via the Vaults Mobile App. Rewards not in Main Wallet Rewards accumulate directly inside the Stake Account, not liquid wallet balance. Staked balance grows inside the Stake Account. Funds return to main wallet upon de-delegation & withdrawal.

docs.title: Q3: RESTful API Standardization & Redesign
docs.text:
This document presents a comprehensive RESTful API Architectural Redesign for three legacy Liminal API endpoints identified in the Technical Writer Evaluation Assignment:

  1. https://docs.lmnl.app/reference/gettransfers (POST /api/wallet/get-transfer-list)
  2. https://docs.lmnl.app/reference/sendmanytransaction (POST /api/wallet/send-many-transaction)
  3. https://docs.lmnl.app/reference/getwalletbalance (POST /api/wallet/balance)

docs.title: Architectural Audit & Non-RESTful Anti-Patterns
docs.text: The three legacy endpoints violate standard REST architectural principles in several key areas:

docs.title: Identified Non-REST Anti-Patterns
docs.text:
1. VERB-IN-PATH & RPC-OVER-HTTP ANTI-PATTERN
   Legacy Docs:   GET/POST  /reference/gettransfers
   Legacy API:    POST      /api/wallet/get-transfer-list
   Legacy Docs:   POST      /reference/sendmanytransaction
   Legacy API:    POST      /api/wallet/send-many-transaction
   Legacy Docs:   GET/POST  /reference/getwalletbalance
   Legacy API:    POST      /api/wallet/balance
   Critique: In REST, the HTTP Verb (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) defines the action. 
             Including verbs ("get", "send") in the URI and using HTTP POST for read-only 
             data queries creates RPC-style endpoints that prevent standard HTTP caching.

2. NON-PLURAL RESOURCE NOUNS
   Legacy:  sendmanytransaction, getwalletbalance
   Critique: REST resources represent collections of entities and should use lowercase, 
             pluralized nouns (e.g. /transfers, /transactions, /wallets).

3. LACK OF SUB-RESOURCE HIERARCHY
   Legacy:  POST /api/wallet/balance (passing wallet ID in body or query)
   Critique: Balances are dependent child attributes of a specific Wallet entity. 
             The URI structure should reflect the resource hierarchy (/wallets/{wallet_id}/balances).

4. INCONSISTENT ERROR SCHEMAS & MISSING IDEMPOTENCY
   Legacy:  Ad-hoc JSON error structures without standardized HTTP status codes or retry safety headers.
   Critique: Modern enterprise APIs mandate RFC 7807 problem details, HTTP 422 status codes for threat screening, and Idempotency-Key headers for financial operations.

docs.title: The Redesigned REST API Suite
docs.text:
The matrix below maps each legacy endpoint to its standardized RESTful equivalent:

Legacy Endpoint (Docs & API Route) Redesigned RESTful Resource URI HTTP Method Resource Description POST /api/wallet/get-transfer-list (/reference/gettransfers) GET /v2/transfers GET Retrieve a paginated collection of historical fund transfers. POST /api/wallet/send-many-transaction (/reference/sendmanytransaction) POST /v2/transfers/batch POST Create a new atomic multi-destination batch transfer resource. POST /api/wallet/balance (/reference/getwalletbalance) GET /v2/wallets/{wallet_id}/balances GET Fetch token balances for a specific vault wallet resource.

docs.title: Legacy vs. Redesigned Comparison
docs.text:
• Legacy: POST /api/wallet/get-transfer-list (Using POST for data fetch)
  • Redesigned: GET https://docs.lmnl.app/v2/transfers

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text:
Use standard REST query parameters for filtering, sorting, and cursor pagination:

Parameter Type Default Description wallet_id string — Filter transfers by source wallet vault ID. status string — Filter by state (PENDING, COMPLETED, FAILED, BLOCKED). asset string — Filter by token asset symbol (e.g. ETH, SOL, USDT). limit integer 50 Maximum items to return per page (Max 250). starting_after string — Cursor object ID for fetching the next page of results.

docs.text:
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "trsf_90812349120",
      "object": "transfer",
      "wallet_id": "vlt_892341029384",
      "amount": "1.500000",
      "asset": "ETH",
      "destination_address": "0x71C7656EC7ab88b098defB751B7401B5f6d8976F",

    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "trsf_90812349120"
}

docs.title: Legacy vs. Redesigned Comparison
docs.text:
• Legacy: POST /api/wallet/send-many-transaction
  • Redesigned: POST https://docs.lmnl.app/v2/transfers/batch

docs.title: Key Architectural Enhancements
docs.text:
1. Idempotency Guarantee: Accepts an Idempotency-Key: <UUIDv4> HTTP header to prevent duplicate payouts caused by network timeouts or automatic retries.
  2. Pluralized Sub-Resource: Grouping under /v2/transfers/batch clearly designates a batch operation on the transfers collection.

docs.title: Request Headers
docs.text:
POST /v2/transfers/batch HTTP/1.1
Host: docs.lmnl.app
Authorization: Bearer liminal_sk_live_98a7sdf98a7sdf98
Idempotency-Key: 7b9e4a12-8c3d-4f5e-9a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b
Content-Type: application/json

docs.title: Legacy vs. Redesigned Comparison
docs.text:
• Legacy: POST /api/wallet/balance (Passing wallet ID in query or body)
  • Redesigned: GET https://docs.lmnl.app/v2/wallets/{wallet_id}/balances

docs.title: Sub-Resource Hierarchy Rationale
docs.text: In REST, a wallet balance cannot exist independently of a wallet entity. Routing via /v2/wallets/{wallet_id}/balances leverages standard REST sub-resource paths, making resource scoping, permissions, and caching straightforward.

docs.title: Standardized Error Payload (RFC 7807 Problem Details)
docs.text:
To eliminate inconsistent error structures, all /v2/ REST endpoints adopt the RFC 7807 Problem Details Specification, including HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity for Cube3 security screening blocks:

{
  "type": "https://docs.lmnl.app/errors/address-threat-detected",
  "title": "Address Threat Blocked",
  "status": 422,
  "detail": "The transaction request was aborted because destination address 0x35febC101123... exceeded the maximum allowed risk score threshold (Risk Score > 80).",
  "instance": "/v2/transfers/batch",
  "code": "RISK_SCREENING_FAILED",
  "invalid_params": [
    {
      "name": "recipients[0].destination_address",
      "reason": "Flagged by Cube3 Security Inspector with Risk Score 99 (Sanctioned / Malicious Activity)",
      "screening_id": 1299
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: OpenAPI 3.0.0 Specification (Redesigned /v2/ REST Suite)
docs.text:
Below is the OpenAPI 3.0.0 definition representing the standardized /v2/ REST API suite:

{
  "openapi": "3.0.0",
  "info": {
    "title": "Liminal REST API v2",
    "version": "2.0.0",
    "description": "Standardized RESTful API suite for Liminal custody, transfers, and wallet management."
  },
  "servers": [
    {
      "url": "https://docs.lmnl.app/v2"
    }
  ],
  "paths": {
    "/transfers": {
      "get": {
        "summary": "Retrieve Transfers Collection",
        "parameters": [
          { "name": "wallet_id", "in": "query", "schema": { "type": "string" } },
          { "name": "status", "in": "query", "schema": { "type": "string" } },
          { "name": "limit", "in": "query", "schema": { "type": "integer", "default": 50 } },
          { "name": "starting_after", "in": "query", "schema": { "type": "string" } }
        ],
        "responses": {
          "200": { "description": "Successful retrieval" }
        }
      }
    },
    "/transfers/batch": {
      "post": {
        "summary": "Create Batch Transfer",
        "parameters": [
          {
            "name": "Idempotency-Key",
            "in": "header",
            "required": true,
            "schema": { "type": "string", "format": "uuid" }
          }
        ],
        "requestBody": {
          "required": true,
          "content": { "application/json": {} }
        },
        "responses": {
          "201": { "description": "Batch transfer created" },
          "422": { "description": "Threat Screening Blocked (RISK_SCREENING_FAILED)" }
        }
      }
    },
    "/wallets/{wallet_id}/balances": {
      "get": {
        "summary": "Retrieve Wallet Balances",
        "parameters": [
          { "name": "wallet_id", "in": "path", "required": true, "schema": { "type": "string" } }
        ],
        "responses": {
          "200": { "description": "Wallet balances fetched" }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: API Migration & Backward Compatibility Strategy
docs.text:
To ensure zero disruption for existing exchange client integrations, Liminal implements a phased Deprecation & Migration Roadmap:

docs.title: HTTP Deprecation Headers
docs.text:
Legacy /v1/ responses will include standard deprecation headers informing clients of the migration window:

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Deprecation: @1790812800
Sunset: Mon, 01 Feb 2027 00:00:00 GMT
Link: <https://docs.lmnl.app/v2/migration-guide>; rel="successor-version"
